faqs.question: What purity grades of sulfuric acid are available for laboratory use in Oman?
faqs.answer: Laboratory sulfuric acid (H₂SO₄) is supplied in several purity grades to match application requirements. ACS (American Chemical Society) reagent grade is 95–98% H₂SO₄ with strict limits on heavy metals, chloride, nitrate, and residue — required for analytical chemistry titrations, pH standards, and trace analysis. AR (Analytical Reagent) grade from BDH, Sigma-Aldrich, or Merck meets equivalent purity for laboratory analysis. Technical grade is 93–98% but with higher impurity levels, suitable for industrial use but not laboratory analytical work. For HPLC mobile phase preparation, ultra-pure (HPLC grade) sulphuric acid with sub-ppb metal contaminant levels is required. In Oman's university and research laboratory sector (SQU, Sultan Qaboos University; UTAS; CAS), analytical grade is standard. For Oman's industrial quality control labs performing wastewater COD analysis (which uses sulphuric acid), AR grade is specified in Standard Methods for the Examination of Water and Wastewater. Global Chemicals LLC supplies laboratory sulfuric acid from international brands (BDH, Sigma, Merck) with lot-specific certificates of analysis.

faqs.question: What safety precautions are required when handling sulfuric acid in an Oman laboratory?
faqs.answer: Sulfuric acid is one of the most dangerous common laboratory chemicals, with unique hazards: it is strongly corrosive (pH<1 at dilute concentrations), generates intense heat on dilution with water (always add acid to water, never water to acid), and concentrated sulfuric acid dehydrates organic materials (including human tissue) causing severe chemical burns with delayed pain onset. In Oman laboratory environments, mandatory safety controls include: chemical-resistant gloves (butyl rubber or neoprene, not nitrile for concentrated acid), chemical splash goggles (not standard safety glasses), lab coat and closed-toe shoes, use only in a fume hood for concentrated acid, designated acid storage in polypropylene or glass secondary containment cabinets, spill kits containing sodium bicarbonate neutraliser, and emergency eyewash within 10 seconds of handling area. For dilution, always add concentrated acid slowly to water while stirring, never the reverse. Oman's Ministry of Manpower OSH regulations require chemical-specific COSHH assessments for hazardous substance use in laboratories. Global Chemicals LLC provides SDS, risk assessment templates, and personal protective equipment alongside laboratory chemical supply.

faqs.question: What are the laboratory applications of hydrochloric acid in Oman?

faqs.question: What are the laboratory and industrial uses of acetone in Oman?
faqs.answer: Acetone (propanone, CAS 67-64-1) is one of the most versatile solvents in both laboratory and industrial settings in Oman. In laboratories, acetone is used for: cleaning glassware (rapidly dissolves most organic residues including oils, greases, adhesives, and many polymer coatings), solvent for organic synthesis and extraction, HPLC solvent and mobile phase component (miscible with water and most organic solvents), TLC (thin layer chromatography) plate development, and drying rinsed glassware before storage (acetone displaces water and evaporates quickly). Industrially, acetone is used in nail varnish removers, paint strippers, fibreglass manufacturing (dissolves polyester resins for cleanup), adhesive formulation (component of contact cements and speciality adhesives), and as a solvent for cellulose acetate, polystyrene, and epoxy resins. In Oman's pharmaceutical and plastics sectors, acetone is a critical process solvent. Flash point is −20°C (extremely flammable, Class IA); storage and use require ATEX-rated environments and grounded metal containers. Laboratory acetone (ACS grade 99.5%+) with water content below 0.02% is available from Global Chemicals LLC in 2.5L and 5L quantities.

faqs.question: What is absolute ethanol and what laboratory applications require it?
faqs.answer: Absolute ethanol (anhydrous ethanol, 200 proof, CAS 64-17-5) is ethanol with water content below 0.1% (99.5%+ purity by GC), produced by azeotropic or molecular sieve dehydration beyond the normal 95.6% ethanol-water azeotrope. The absence of water makes it essential for applications where any water contamination causes problems: DNA/RNA precipitation and washing in molecular biology (water inhibits alcohol precipitation of nucleic acids); Karl Fischer water content titration (absolute ethanol is the titration solvent); dehydration steps in histology tissue processing (serial dilutions from 70% to 100% ethanol dehydrate tissue before paraffin embedding); anhydrous organic synthesis reactions (Grignard, esterification) where water causes side reactions; spectroscopic standards preparation (water has UV and IR absorptions that interfere); and absolute ethanol is the certified vehicle for many pharmaceutical reference standards. For Oman's university chemistry, biology, and medical laboratory sectors, absolute ethanol from Sigma-Aldrich, Merck, or BDH is the preferred choice. Global Chemicals LLC supplies laboratory absolute ethanol with molecular sieve packaging to prevent atmospheric moisture uptake.

title: EDTA Disodium Salt (Laboratory Grade)
description: High-purity EDTA for chelation, buffer preparation, and molecular biology.

details.longDescription:
EDTA disodium salt dihydrate (Na2EDTA·2H2O, C10H14N2Na2O8·2H2O, CAS 6381-92-6, formula weight 372.24) is the laboratory chelating agent that binds calcium, magnesium, iron and other metal ions into stable complexes. Global Chemicals LLC supplies it at 99% minimum purity, DNase- and RNase-free, as a white crystalline powder in 100 g, 500 g, 1 kg and 5 kg containers, from stock in Muscat, with a certificate of analysis and safety data sheet for every lot.

Analytical use. Disodium EDTA is the titrant of complexometric titration: a 0.01 M solution titrated against Eriochrome Black T at pH 10 measures total hardness, and 1 mL of 0.01 M EDTA corresponds to 1 mg of calcium carbonate. Oman's water-quality laboratories use it for drinking water, irrigation water, boiler feedwater and cooling-tower water; industrial QC labs use it for calcium in cement and gypsum and for metal determinations, and it serves as a standard for atomic-absorption calibration checks. Environmental labs use it to mobilise heavy metals for analysis.

Molecular biology use. EDTA inhibits metal-dependent nucleases, so it protects DNA and RNA in extraction, storage and electrophoresis. The standard 0.5 M stock is made by dissolving 186.1 g of the dihydrate per litre while raising the pH to 8.0 with sodium hydroxide; the salt does not dissolve fully until the pH reaches about 8. From that stock come TE buffer (10 mM Tris, 1 mM EDTA), TAE and TBE running buffers, enzyme storage buffers and protein-purification buffers. It is also the anticoagulant in blood-collection tubes and a stabiliser in biological media.

A 1% solution has a pH of 4–6; the powder is stable indefinitely when kept dry and closed. It is not hazardous to handle beyond ordinary dust precautions. Laboratories ordering regularly can hold a standing order so the same lot stays in use across a validation period.

title: Agar Bacteriological (Laboratory Grade)
description: High-purity bacteriological agar for microbiology culture media.

details.longDescription:
Bacteriological agar (CAS 9002-18-0) is the purified polysaccharide extracted from red seaweed that sets microbiological culture media into a firm, clear gel that bacteria cannot digest. Global Chemicals LLC supplies the bacteriological grade from stock in Muscat in 100 g, 500 g and 1 kg containers, with a gel strength of 600–700 g/cm², a gelling temperature of about 40 °C, a melting temperature of about 85 °C and a low content of salts and nutrients, so the agar itself adds nothing to the medium it sets.

Those numbers are what the laboratory relies on. Because agar melts at 85 °C but does not set until it cools to 40 °C, media can be held molten at 45–50 °C while heat-sensitive supplements such as blood, antibiotics or sugars are added, then poured into plates and slants that stay solid at incubator temperatures up to 45 °C. The usual concentration is 15 g/L (1.5%); 7–10 g/L gives a soft motility or semi-solid medium and 20 g/L a firm surface for streaking. Dissolve the powder by boiling with stirring before autoclaving at 121 °C for 15 minutes; repeated re-melting weakens the gel, so melt only what will be poured.

Oman's hospital diagnostic laboratories, food-safety and seafood-testing laboratories, water-quality laboratories, pharmaceutical QC and university microbiology departments use it to prepare nutrient agar, blood agar, MacConkey agar, Mueller-Hinton agar for antibiotic sensitivity testing, and selective media such as TCBS for Vibrio detection in seafood, as well as plate-count and membrane-filtration media for water analysis.

Each lot ships with a certificate of analysis stating gel strength, gelling and melting points, moisture, ash and microbial purity, plus a safety data sheet; endotoxin and inhibitor data are available for cell-culture and pharmaceutical users. Store the powder dry and closed at room temperature; it keeps for years. For the full reagent list, grades and documentation, see the laboratory chemicals supplier guide linked on this page.
